raw_response:
I am 70 years old. My back aches by afternoon. Three of my children work in Handan or further away, and my husband is getting on in years too. I cannot do what I could do at 50. But I have farmed this land for 15 years and I know it. The soil here is heavy clay loam, the water table is reachable with my electric pump. The government promoted the wheat-maize rotation years ago and I have followed it because it makes sense — the wheat stubble feeds the summer maize, and I can rent the combine for both harvests.

For my **8 mu of wheat-maize land**, I will plant wheat in October after I have my son-in-law come back to do rotary tillage — I am not ploughing deep anymore, it is too hard on machinery and my budget. I will use the improved Jimai variety seed that the village supply cooperative sells. I know it. I have used it for three years. I will apply base fertilizer before sowing — compound fertilizer plus extra urea. In spring I will topdress nitrogen at jointing stage. I pump irrigation water from my well three times: once before winter dormancy, once at jointing, once at grain fill. I spray herbicide once in early spring, and one more time for aphids before heading. I expect around 450 jin per mu — nothing special, but reliable.

After the wheat combine leaves in early June, I will direct-seed maize the same day or next. No-tillage into the stubble. I use the hybrid seed — Xianyu 335 or whatever the cooperative has. Maize is easier. I irrigate twice, at emergence if dry and at tasseling. Two pesticide passes for corn borer and fall armyworm. My son helped me get a smart phone app that shows forecast rain so I don't waste pump water. I expect around 550 jin per mu.

For the **2.1 mu of cotton**, I keep it because it gives me cash in hand in autumn when prices are reasonable, and I can pick it at my own pace across many mornings. But I am honest with myself — I am not increasing the cotton area. The picking is hard. I will spring-plough that plot myself with the small walking tractor. I use improved cotton seed, not the expensive hybrid. I apply more potassium on cotton because it needs it here. I irrigate three times and spray five times for aphids, bollworm, and spider mites — cotton always needs more sprays. I expect about 250 jin of seed cotton per mu. Not great, but manageable alone.
